scope: Disposable local fixtures only; no production services, customer files, real credentials, provider APIs, signing operations, networks, or physical devices.

runs.name: gateway-and-native-boundary
runs.environment: Production-mode FastAPI TestClient, disposable local PostgreSQL, temporary account/workspace roots, existing local hostd/libchudware build chudcode-runtime-v0.4.3-5-g92a4ebb71-dirty, fake OPENAI_API_KEY sentinel

observations.qualification: This proves no server Origin rejection. SameSite=Lax plus browser CORS/preflight controls mean it is not, alone, proof of a cross-site browser exploit.

observations.scenario: shared native daemon reachable by standard tenant
NUL path reads outside tenant root
standard tenant can request host process spawn
suspension invalidates active access while suspended

runs.name: identity-and-billing-state
runs.environment: Production-mode FastAPI TestClient and disposable local PostgreSQL; genuine local OAuth state/cookie transaction with only provider identity resolution replaced by a fixed fixture; no provider or Stripe network call

observations.scenario: genuine local OAuth state transaction completed
preregistered attacker password activated by OAuth
dormant session survives suspend then reinstate

runs.name: restricted-predicate
runs.environment: In-process services.dag.verify with a temporary marker file

observations.scenario: advertised restricted predicate performs file I/O through abs.__self__

runs.name: model-code-execution
runs.environment: In-process services.kernel_exec with build123d namespace replaced by an empty fixture to avoid geometry work and a temporary marker target

observations.scenario: model code receives unrestricted Python builtins

important_limits: The hostd binary was an existing dirty local build; source review covered the current dirty worktree, so runtime evidence proves the observed build behavior but is not an immutable clean-commit attestation.

No attempt was made to crash the daemon, exhaust memory/disk/CPU, contact internal addresses, invoke a real provider, start a real shell, run firmware/emulators, write print media, flash hardware, or exercise physical manufacturing.

Windows-only, macOS-only, live CI, private runtime internals, cloud-edge policy, installed service units, firewall/SSH, provider revocation, backup restoration, and customer-impact logs were not available for runtime verification.
